ssim.note: Reported and tracked on every run, but not a gate until the cross-engine noise floor is calibrated. A pixel floor plus a geometry gate can accept a screen that SSIM alone would reject for anti-aliasing, which is the correct trade here.

geometry.note: Every text node and key container in the web geometry dump must have a matching Compose semantics node within tolerance.

noiseFloor.note: Measured before any port work. If a re-render of the same side already scores below these numbers, the capture is not deterministic and must be fixed before diffing across platforms.

masks.note: Dynamic regions (clocks, progress timers, random ids) are masked per screen in the screen spec, never globally.

criteria: geometry gate passes (key node positions and sizes within tolerance; % of nodes matched is reported)
every remaining residual pixel is explained by a declared residual category
acceptance.whyGeometry: A 95% pixel match can hide a whole block in the wrong place: a 393x852 screen is ~335k pixels, so 5% is ~17k pixels, which is more than a title and a two-line paragraph. Position and size are therefore gated separately from colour.
acceptance.note: SSIM is deliberately excluded from the gate: it is a structural score that reacts to anti-aliasing and text rasterisation, which are engine differences rather than port defects.

residualCategories.note: A screen above the pixel floor with an unexplained residual is not accepted: it is `building` until the residual is named, because an unnamed residual is an unexamined defect.

loops.note: Hard caps. Hitting a cap marks the item blocked and asks the user instead of looping forever.
